content: Diphenoxylate and atropine are prescribed to manage diarrhea. In some cases, this medication may be used for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. This medication is available in tablet and liquid forms, both of which are taken orally. It is typically taken as needed, up to four times a day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. The liquid form comes with a special dropper for accurate dosing. Use the dropper to measure the exact dose, and consult your pharmacist if you are unsure how to measure it properly. Be aware that diphenoxylate has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed by your doctor. Abruptly stopping the medication after prolonged use may lead to withdrawal symptoms, which can include muscle cramps, stomach cramps, unusual sweating, nausea, vomiting, and trembling. Before starting diphenoxylate and atropine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to either of these drugs or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially MAO inhibitors, muscle relaxants, narcotic cough or pain relievers, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of chronic lung disease, ulcerative colitis, liver disease, or alcohol abuse. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Before undergoing any surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Be aware that this drug may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Additionally, alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. If you miss a scheduled dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Diphenoxylate and atropine may cause side effects. To alleviate thirst and dry mouth, drink plenty of fluids, chew gum, or suck on sugarless hard candies. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: severe nausea and vomiting, severe stomach pain, bloating, extreme drowsiness, palpitations, swelling, rash, loss of appetite, dryness of the skin, nose, or mouth, difficulty breathing, or seizures. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor to monitor your response to this medication. Do not give this medication to children under 2 years of age. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your diarrhea does not improve within two days or worsens, contact your doctor.
